$comment: The capabilities both clients ask for, and the rules a name must satisfy. Read by tests/main/capnames.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest, so the desktop and the phone cannot drift apart. Only advertised capabilities are actually requested, which is why a wrong name here fails silently rather than loudly.

rules.lowercase: Capability names are case-sensitive and every registered one is lowercase. UTF8ONLY is the ISUPPORT token, not a capability.
rules.noClientTagPrefix: A '+' prefixes a message tag. A CAP REQ token starting with one names a capability that cannot exist.
rules.isupportNotCapability: Bot mode, account extbans and WHOX are announced with the ISUPPORT tokens BOT, ACCOUNTEXTBAN and WHOX. None of them is a capability, so asking for one is asking for something that cannot be granted — and because only advertised names are ever requested, it fails by doing nothing rather than by saying so.

deliberatelyNotRequested.draft/persistence: A real capability, and nothing here implements the PERSISTENCE command. Enabling it changes what a server does when a client goes away, which is not something to ask for and then ignore.

$aliases: Capabilities that go by more than one name. A client that knows only one negotiates nothing and the feature is quietly absent — soju offers soju.im/webpush and we asked for draft/webpush, so push through a soju never worked. Read by tests/shared/capnames.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest.

aliases.name: the draft spelling, preferred where both are there
a near miss is a miss
